tasks.title: Add project-scoped source access and revision-safe file saves
tasks.description:
Outcome: Explicit workspace source access and safe expected-revision saves.

Current implementation: The server currently infers source root from planRoot, which fails when the planner moves to HOME.

Implementation responsibility:
- Expose source tree/content/history APIs against the registered workspace, not database location; enforce path containment and deliberate symlink policy.
- Identify saved source, dirty baseline, historical snapshot and draft separately with content/revision fingerprints.
- Implement atomic conflict-aware save using expected source revision and preserving an external/agent edit; provide reviewable conflict results.
- Handle deleted/moved files, binary/large content, readonly/historical views and unavailable local/remote workspace explicitly.
- Notify affected analysis/graph owners without automatically committing code or overwriting foreign edits.

Acceptance and evidence:
- A database outside the project cannot redirect source access into HOME or the wrong checkout.
- Concurrent editor/agent edits preserve both versions and refuse silent overwrite.
- Source context remains project/workspace/revision explicit across clients.

tasks.title: Share language-server processes across agents and the editor
tasks.description:
Outcome: One compatible analysis runtime shared by agent and editor consumers.

Current implementation: Adding Monaco must not spawn a second LSP for the same effective workspace/configuration, while unrelated workspaces may require different processes.

Implementation responsibility:
- Define broker keys from project/workspace, provider/version and effective build/configuration; atomically coordinate startup/reuse across host processes.
- Own upstream lifecycle, cancellation, consumer attach/detach and recovery in the common service/provider boundary.
- Name document revisions and separate incompatible unsaved overlays; one browser draft cannot overwrite another consumer document state.
- Expose normalized capabilities/navigation/diagnostics through common APIs. A frontend LSP bridge must not initialize a competing runtime independently.
- Verify two agents plus editor, crashed owner, config drift and unsupported semantic operations using isolated compatible provider fixtures.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Compatible consumers reuse one runtime; incompatible keys are explicitly separate.
- Closing the editor does not stop a provider still used by agents.
- Syntax-only capability is not labelled semantic support.
